question_english: According to reinforcement theories of motivation, what is the direct cause-and-effect relationship of administering a timely reward following a teacher’s exceptional pedagogical intervention?
options_english: It reduces the teacher’s intrinsic motivation to teach.
It causes immediate resentment among all other staff members, reducing overall school efficiency.
It neutralizes the need for future administrative supervision.
It increases the probability that the exceptional teaching behavior will be repeated.
explanation_english: The correct answer is that it increases the probability that the exceptional teaching behavior will be repeated. Under Skinnerian reinforcement theories of motivation, administering positive reinforcement immediately after a target behavior strengthens the psychological link between the action and its positive outcome. Timely recognition or rewarding of exceptional pedagogical interventions increases the likelihood that the teacher will repeat that effective behavior, while simultaneously signaling institutional priorities and performance expectations to the broader school faculty.

question_english: What does the “Overjustification Effect” suggest regarding the relationship between intrinsic and extrinsic rewards?

question_english: Identify the correct pair that maps the extrinsic reward to its operational mechanism.
options_english: Promotion – Systematically increases intrinsic job dissatisfaction among senior staff
Pay increment – Acts as a mandatory non-statutory extra-mural welfare measure
Appreciation Letter – Serves as non-monetary formal recognition
Group insurance – Serves as an immediate performance-based annual cash bonus
explanation_english: The correct option is the Appreciation Letter, which serves as a non-monetary formal recognition mechanism. An official appreciation letter issued by school administration represents a classic non-monetary formal recognition mechanism. It provides documented validation of an employee’s extraordinary performance or contributions without involving direct financial transactions. Placed in service records or presented publicly, it satisfies esteem needs, boosts professional morale, and serves as a permanent administrative acknowledgment of merit.

question_english: What is a common cause-and-effect outcome of heavily relying on competitive extrinsic rewards (e.g., “Best Teacher” cash prize) in a school?
options_english: It permanently eliminates all potential interpersonal conflict among teaching staff members across departments.
It dramatically enhances intrinsic motivation across the entire teaching faculty simultaneously and permanently.
It immediately and fully satisfies all statutory compliance requirements of the Directorate of Education.
It causes short-term performance spikes but reduces collaboration and increases professional jealousy.
explanation_english: The correct answer is that it causes short-term performance spikes but reduces collaboration and increases professional jealousy. Heavily relying on competitive extrinsic rewards where employees compete for limited prizes often creates dysfunctional organizational dynamics. While such contests may generate temporary individual effort spikes, they frequently destroy collaborative staff relationships, promote information hoarding, increase interpersonal tension, and foster professional jealousy, ultimately damaging overall institutional cohesiveness and school culture over time.
explanation_hindi: सही उत्तर (d) है। यह अल्पकालिक प्रदर्शन में वृद्धि करता है लेकिन सहयोग को कम करता है और पेशेवर जलन को बढ़ाता है। प्रतिस्पर्धात्मक बाह्य पुरस्कारों पर अत्यधिक निर्भरता, जहां कर्मचारी सीमित पुरस्कारों के लिए प्रतिस्पर्धा करते हैं, अक्सर अस्वस्थ संगठनात्मक गतिशीलता का निर्माण करती है। जबकि ऐसे प्रतियोगिताएं अस्थायी व्यक्तिगत प्रयास में वृद्धि उत्पन्न कर सकती हैं, वे अक्सर सहयोगी कर्मचारी संबंधों को नष्ट कर देती हैं, जानकारी को छिपाने को बढ़ावा देती हैं, अंतःव्यक्तिगत तनाव को बढ़ाती हैं, और पेशेवर जलन को बढ़ावा देती हैं, जो अंततः समय के साथ समग्र संस्थागत एकता और विद्यालय संस्कृति को नुकसान पहुंचाती है।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (D) It causes short-term performance spikes but reduces collaboration and increases professional jealousy.

question_english:
Which of the following characteristics define an
     effectively designed extrinsic reward system in
     an educational institution?
     I. The criteria for earning the reward are
          transparent and objective.
     II. The reward is attainable by anyone who
          meets the specific standard.
     III. The reward is strictly limited to teaching
          staff, excluding non-teaching staff.
     IV. The reward is meaningful and valued by the
          recipients.
     Which of the above statement(s) is/are correct?
options_english: I, II, and III only
I, II, and IV only
II, III, and IV only
I, III, and IV only
explanation_english:
An effective extrinsic reward system requires
       transparent and objective eligibility criteria,
       equal accessibility for all staff meeting established
       standards, and meaningful value to recipients.
       Excluding non-teaching staff arbitrarily creates
       unnecessary organizational divides. Inclusive
       systems that recognize both academic and
       non-academic personnel ensure fairness, boost
       overall institutional morale, and maintain strong
       organizational alignment.
explanation_hindi: सही उत्तर (b) है। एक प्रभावी बाह्य पुरस्कार प्रणाली के लिए पारदर्शी और वस्तुनिष्ठ पात्रता मानदंड, स्थापित मानकों को पूरा करने वाले सभी स्टाफ के लिए समान पहुंच, और प्राप्तकर्ताओं के लिए अर्थपूर्ण मूल्य की आवश्यकता होती है। गैर-शिक्षण स्टाफ को बाहर करना अनावश्यक संगठनात्मक विभाजन उत्पन्न करता है। ऐसे समावेशी प्रणाली जो शैक्षणिक और गैर-शैक्षणिक दोनों कर्मचारियों को मान्यता देती हैं, निष्पक्षता सुनिश्चित करती हैं, समग्र संस्थागत मनोबल को बढ़ाती हैं, और मजबूत संगठनात्मक संरेखण बनाए रखती हैं।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (B) I, II, and IV only

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: An effective extrinsic reward system requires transparent and objective eligibility criteria, equal accessibility for all staff meeting established standards, and meaningful value to recipients.

question_english:
What fundamentally distinguishes monetary
     rewards from non-monetary rewards?
options_english: Monetary rewards are strictly statutory obligations, whereas non-monetary rewards are categorized as illegal administrative practices.
Monetary rewards have direct financial value, while non-monetary rewards provide value without direct cash transfer.
Monetary rewards can only be disbursed upon retirement, while non-monetary rewards are given strictly during active service.
Non-monetary rewards require formal Finance Ministry approval, whereas monetary rewards do not require higher administrative consent.
explanation_english:
Monetary rewards involve direct financial
       transfers or cash-equivalent benefits that
       increase an employee’s disposable income, such
       as performance bonuses, increments, and cash
       prizes. In contrast, non-monetary rewards deliver
       professional or psychological value through non-
       financial means, such as public recognition,
       flexible scheduling, improved facilities, and
       career growth opportunities, without adding
       direct cash to compensation.
explanation_hindi: सही उत्तर (b) है। धनात्मक पुरस्कार सीधे वित्तीय हस्तांतरण या नकद-समान लाभों को शामिल करते हैं जो कर्मचारी की खर्च योग्य आय को बढ़ाते हैं, जैसे प्रदर्शन बोनस, वृद्धि, और नकद पुरस्कार। इसके विपरीत, गैर-धनात्मक पुरस्कार पेशेवर या मनोवैज्ञानिक मूल्य प्रदान करते हैं जो गैर-वित्तीय साधनों के माध्यम से होते हैं, जैसे सार्वजनिक मान्यता, लचीला कार्यक्रम, बेहतर सुविधाएँ, और करियर विकास के अवसर, बिना सीधे नकद को मुआवजे में जोड़ने के।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (B) Monetary rewards have direct financial value

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: Monetary rewards involve direct financial transfers or cash-equivalent benefits that increase an employee’s disposable income, such as performance bonuses, increments, and cash prizes.

question_english:

    over monetary rewards?

question_english:
Under the provisions of the CCS (Conduct) Rules regarding the acceptance of awards from private organizations, which of the following conditions must typically be met?
I. The award should not have a substantial monetary component without prior approval.
II. The organization giving the award should not have any official dealings with the teacher in their official capacity.
III. The teacher must not use their official position to solicit the award.
Which of the above statement(s) is/are correct?
options_english: I and II only
II and III only
I and III only
I, II, and III
explanation_english: The correct option is 'I, II, and III'. Accepting external awards under Central Civil Services Conduct Rules requires ensuring that the award lacks unauthorized monetary components, that the presenting private organization has no official dealings with the employee, and that the employee did not leverage their position. key_facts: Printed answer key: (D) I, II, and III

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: Accepting external awards under Central Civil Services Conduct Rules requires ensuring that the award lacks unauthorized monetary components, that the presenting private organization has no official dealings with the employee, and that the employee did not leverage their position.
